what.text: Dapoxetine is a short-acting SSRI (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor), the same drug family as many antidepressants. It is a tablet, sold in Europe under the brand Priligy, and approved for use as needed before sex rather than every day.

src.label: Priligy summary of product characteristics (Spanish), AEMPS CIMA

what.text: Ejaculation is controlled by a reflex centre in the spinal cord. The European label says dapoxetine is thought to act by blocking the reuptake of serotonin, a nerve messenger, which delays this reflex. In rats it slowed the ejaculation reflex.

src.label: Priligy summary of product characteristics (Spanish), AEMPS CIMA

what.text: In Europe it is approved only for premature ejaculation (PE) in men aged 18 to 64 who meet strict criteria, including ejaculating within 2 minutes of penetration, with marked distress and poor control.

src.label: Priligy summary of product characteristics (Spanish), AEMPS CIMA

what.text: Dapoxetine is approved in Spain, Ireland and other countries, but it is not approved in the US.

research.text: Dapoxetine was tested in five randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trials with 6,081 men in more than 25 countries, lasting 9 to 24 weeks. The main measure was time from penetration to ejaculation, timed by stopwatch. The trials were run by the drug’s developers (ALZA, then Johnson & Johnson).

research.title: Two US trials, 2,614 men, 12 weeks

facts.v: two identical randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trials, analyzed together
men with moderate-to-severe PE in stable relationships: 870 placebo, 874 on 30 mg, 870 on 60 mg; 121 US sites
12 weeks, taken 1 to 3 hours before sex
time to ejaculation by stopwatch; side effects

research.found: Average time to ejaculation rose from about 0.9 minutes to 1.75 minutes on placebo, 2.78 minutes on 30 mg and 3.32 minutes on 60 mg. Nausea was the most common side effect (8.7% on 30 mg, 20.1% on 60 mg).

research.title: International trial, 1,162 men, 24 weeks

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial
1,162 men with PE in long-term relationships; 618 completed
time to ejaculation by stopwatch; control, distress and satisfaction scores; side effects

research.found: Average time rose from 0.9 minutes to 1.9 minutes on placebo, 3.2 minutes on 30 mg and 3.5 minutes on 60 mg. Side effects led 1.3%, 3.9% and 8.2% of men to stop. The European label reports that 28.4% (30 mg) and 35.5% (60 mg) rated their PE “better” or “much better” at 24 weeks, versus 14% on placebo.

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial
1,067 men with PE in monogamous relationships; 858 completed
time to ejaculation by stopwatch; PE scores; side effects

research.found: Average time rose from about 1.1 minutes to 2.4 minutes on placebo, 3.9 minutes on 30 mg and 4.2 minutes on 60 mg. Side effects led 0.3%, 1.7% and 5.1% to stop.

src.label: McMahon C, et al. J Sex Med 2010

research.title: All five Phase III trials together, 6,081 men

facts.v: pooled analysis of five randomized, placebo-controlled trials
time to ejaculation, PE scores, mood and withdrawal checks, side effects

research.found: At 12 weeks, average time was 1.9 minutes on placebo, 3.1 minutes on 30 mg and 3.6 minutes on 60 mg, from 0.9 minutes at the start. The most common side effects were nausea, dizziness and headache. The authors found no anxiety, suicidality or withdrawal syndrome on the scales they used.

research.text: Men with erectile dysfunction or other sexual problems, and men with heart disease, were left out of the Phase III trials.

world.lead: Dapoxetine (Priligy) is an approved, prescription-only medicine in Spain (since 2009) and Ireland (since 2012), through national approvals rather than one EU-wide approval. It is prescription-only in Australia. It is not approved in the US, and Canada’s drug database lists no dapoxetine product.

after.text: Dapoxetine is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It does not fall in any listed class, and S0 covers only drugs with no approval anywhere, which does not apply to dapoxetine.

side.text: The European label lists fainting (syncope) and a drop in blood pressure on standing as the main warnings. Nausea, dizziness, headache and diarrhoea were the most common side effects in the Phase III trials, and all were more common at 60 mg than 30 mg.

items.text: nausea 11.0% / 22.2%, dizziness 5.8% / 10.9%, headache 5.6% / 8.8%, diarrhoea 3.5% / 6.9%, insomnia 2.1% / 3.9%, tiredness 2.0% / 4.1%.
